title: Cruising & First Steps
strapline: Pulling up, edging along the furniture, letting go for one wobbly step — the biggest journey a baby ever makes.
intent: Support babies through the great transition from crawling to walking — pulling up, cruising, standing and those first independent steps.
Provide sturdy things to pull up on and cruise along, giving safe handholds that build leg strength and balance.
Offer moving handholds — push-along toys and low walkers — that lend confidence to the earliest steps.
Build the balance, core strength and nerve that walking asks for, at each baby's own pace, never rushed.
Celebrate every stage — the first pull-up, the first cruise, the first let-go — as the milestone it truly is.
implementation: Arrange sturdy, stable furniture and low rails at just the right height for pulling up and cruising along.
Set treasures along a low surface so a baby edges sideways from one to the next — cruising with a purpose.
Offer weighted push-along walkers and prams that won't shoot away, for babies ready to step behind a moving handhold.
Leave gaps to bridge — a short, tempting distance between two sofas — so a baby lets go and reaches across.
Stay close for the wobbles, keep the floor soft and clear, and follow each baby's readiness rather than a timetable.
key_questions: Can you pull yourself all the way up to standing?
Shall you cruise along to reach the next treasure?
Can you let go with one hand — look at you balancing!
Will you take a step across to me?
Off you go, pushing the walker — where are we walking to?

impact.text: Babies gain control of their bodies in sequence — pulling up, cruising, standing and taking their first steps.
A baby pulls up, cruises the furniture and explores standing, working the whole body freely and hard.
The most confident walkers begin to toddle across open floor, running the earliest steps into real walking.
With their key person close for the wobbles, a baby dares to let go and step, returning for a steadying hand.

enhancements: A low cruising rail or sturdy sofa line with treasures set along the top.
Weighted push-along walkers and prams that resist shooting away.
A short, safe gap between two stable supports to tempt a first let-go.
A low mirror at standing height to greet a newly-upright baby.
A soft, clear floor zone kept just for pulling up, cruising and stepping.

playing_exploring: The baby explores standing and stepping on their own terms, choosing when to pull up and let go.
Whole-body balance and movement are the play, tried again and again.
active_learning: Babies persist through countless wobbles and sit-downs, thrilled by each new pull-up and step.
creating_thinking: A baby judges the gap, gathers their nerve and tries a step — connecting their own effort to moving forward.
